claims.claim: The fixed-k problems are monotone under padding: k-Induced Disjoint Paths reduces to ℓ-Induced Disjoint Paths for every fixed ℓ≥k while preserving H3-freeness. Moreover, k=1 is linear-time solvable and every fixed-k problem is in NP.
claims.evidence: Adding ℓ−k isolated K2 components forces the added terminal paths and preserves the answer. Since H3 is connected and has eight vertices, the disjoint K2 components neither create nor destroy an H3 subgraph. For k=1, connectivity is necessary and sufficient; a shortest connecting path has no chord and BFS/DFS is linear. Explicit path lists are polynomial certificates whose disjointness and forbidden cross-edges are directly checkable.
claims.witness: The padding gadget is one isolated K2 for each added terminal pair.
claims.search_method: Direct two-direction reduction audit, shortest-path argument, and certificate-size verification.

claims.claim: Every H3-free graph is 6-degenerate, with the constant sharp; additionally, two vertices of degree at least three can never be at distance exactly three. Thus an n-vertex H3-free graph has at most 6n−21 edges for n≥7, and every connected H3-free graph of minimum degree at least three has diameter at most two.
claims.evidence: On a shortest length-three path u-x-y-v between degree-at-least-three endpoints, each endpoint has two further neighbors. Shortestness keeps those four neighbors outside the central path and pairwise distinct across the two sides, producing H3 as a subgraph. Any minimum-degree-seven graph greedily contains every eight-vertex tree, including H3, so every subgraph of an H3-free graph has a vertex of degree at most six. The standard degeneracy sum gives 6n−21 edges. K7 proves sharpness, and a geodesic prefix of length three proves the diameter consequence.
claims.witness: K7 is H3-free because it has seven vertices and has degeneracy six.
claims.search_method: Direct extremal and geodesic proof audit, including all distinctness conditions in the H3 embedding.

claims.claim: H3-free graphs admit an arbitrary-routing-plus-matching normal form. Let R be any graph and M a matching on V(R), disjoint from E(R). Replace every edge of R by a four-edge path and retain every edge of M unsubdivided, obtaining G(R,M). Then G(R,M) is H3-free. With all terminals in V(R), induced linkages in G(R,M) correspond exactly to vertex-disjoint paths in R∪M such that every M-edge whose two endpoints are selected is itself used between consecutive vertices of one path. In particular, the H3-free class has unbounded treewidth.
claims.evidence: The degree-three centers of an H3 copy would have to be original vertices. A three-edge path starting through an R-corridor cannot reach another original vertex, while one starting through M cannot use a second matching edge and has only two remaining corridor steps. Thus no possible H3 center path exists. Paths with original endpoints traverse every entered corridor completely. Projection and lifting are inverse, and the only possible forbidden selected-vertex adjacencies not encoded by path use are M-edges, exactly yielding the stated matching-clean condition. With M empty and R=K_m, contraction of the corridors gives a K_m minor and unbounded treewidth.
claims.witness: M=∅ and R=K_m yield H3-free graphs containing K_m as a minor.
claims.search_method: Universal structural proof plus exhaustive projection-set comparison for every representation on at most four original vertices.

claims.claim: Conditional contraction lemma: if R and M are supplied, M is a matching on V(R) disjoint from E(R), G=G(R,M), and all terminals are distinct vertices of V(R), then preprocessing matching edges with two terminal endpoints and contracting every remaining edge of M reduces induced linkage in G exactly to ordinary vertex-disjoint linkage in a quotient graph. Consequently, for every fixed k this represented-input, original-terminal problem is polynomial-time solvable.
claims.evidence: A matching edge joining terminals of different pairs makes matching-cleanliness impossible; one equal to a prescribed pair forces that one-edge path and can be removed with its endpoints. Every remaining matched class contains at most one terminal. Clean paths contract to disjoint quotient paths. Conversely, at each visited matched class, quotient edges incident at one port lift through that endpoint, while opposite ports lift through the matching edge; terminal classes are handled from the actual terminal port. This produces precisely matching-clean disjoint paths. Four-subdividing the quotient converts ordinary linkage to induced linkage in an H1-subgraph-free graph, so the source-stated fixed-k polynomial algorithm applies.
claims.search_method: Port-by-port inverse-map proof and exhaustive comparison of matching-clean versus quotient existence over 252399 represented terminal instances on at most five original vertices.

claims.claim: The conditional contraction lemma does not establish polynomial-time solvability for standard instances on the entire graph class {G(R,M)}: a standard instance supplies only G, may put terminals at subdivision vertices, and need not determine a unique R,M representation. Therefore the classification for every fixed k≥2 remains open in this draft.
claims.evidence: Internal terminals on a four-edge corridor are valid standard-instance terminals but have no vertices in the projected R∪M instance. Moreover, the same labeled P6 has valid representations with 0-1-2-3-4 as the corridor and 4-5 as M, or with 1-2-3-4-5 as the corridor and 0-1 as M. Thus the conditional proof assumes information and terminal placement absent from the standard model. The draft supplies neither representation recovery/general terminal handling nor a full-class algorithm or hardness reduction for k≥2, so its explicitly draft-relative open-status statement is accurate.
claims.witness: A P5 corridor with internal terminals demonstrates the terminal-scope gap; labeled P6 demonstrates nonunique representations.
claims.search_method: Input-model comparison and direct validation of both explicit representations.

claims.claim: Four is the sharp universal corridor length in the arbitrary-routing-plus-matching construction: replacing every R-edge by a path of any fixed length d≥4 always produces an H3-free graph after retaining M, whereas each d∈{1,2,3} has a permitted pair (R,M) whose resulting graph contains H3.
claims.evidence: For d≥4, subdivision vertices cannot be H3 centers, and no three-edge path can run between original centers: a corridor needs at least four edges, while after an initial matching edge the matching property forces the remaining steps into a corridor. For d=1, R=H3 suffices. For d=3, a subdivided edge of R=K4 supplies the center path and the other incident corridors supply four leaves. For d=2, the stated R edges up,uq,vw,wr,ws together with M={uv} give center path u-v-a-w and four distinct corridor leaves.
claims.witness: Explicit H3-producing instances are R=H3,M=∅ for d=1; the stated seven-original construction for d=2; and R=K4,M=∅ for d=3.
claims.search_method: Universal center-distance proof, explicit witness reconstruction, and exact H3 detection on the witnesses and 656 small d=4,5 representations.

claims.claim: For arbitrary graphs, hence also for H3-free graphs, k-Induced Disjoint Paths is fixed-parameter tractable in k+b, where b is the number of vertices of degree at least three. There is an exact equivalent compression with at most b+binom(b,2)+6k vertices.
claims.evidence: After deleting B, every component has maximum degree two and at most two attachments. A terminal-free usable component must join distinct B vertices, and one two-edge representative per unordered B-pair suffices. In terminal-bearing components, the terminals and attachment occurrences divide the path or cycle into all-or-nothing gaps. Retaining length-one gaps and shortening longer gaps to length two preserves precisely endpoint adjacency, hence also chords, cross-path edges, disjointness, and liftability. There are at most b+2k marked vertices, binom(b,2) generic representatives, and at most 4k gap representatives. Brute-force solution of the bounded compressed instance followed by expansion is FPT in k+b.
claims.search_method: Component-by-component proof, count audit, and exhaustive compression-equivalence testing over 26202 terminal instances from all graphs on at most five vertices.

claims.claim: A globally shortest path for one terminal pair cannot be fixed greedily, even on a seven-vertex H3-free graph.
claims.evidence: The listed seven-vertex graph is automatically H3-subgraph-free because H3 has eight vertices. Paths s1-y-z-t1 and s2-t2 are vertex-disjoint with no cross-edge. The sole length-two s1-t1 path is s1-x-t1, hence it is uniquely globally shortest, but xs2 is a forbidden cross-edge with the forced s2-t2 path. Thus fixing that shortest path changes a YES instance to failure.
claims.search_method: Direct path enumeration and exact witness verification.

claims.claim: The seven-vertex obstruction is vertex-minimal for the unique-shortest formulation and also defeats total-length minimization: no graph on at most six vertices with four distinct terminals has an induced linkage while the first pair's unique globally shortest path is unextendable, and in the seven-vertex witness the unique minimum-total-length ordinary two-linkage is not induced.
claims.evidence: If an induced linkage P1,P2 exists but the unique shortest first path Q is unextendable, Q differs from P1 and is strictly shorter. P1 must have at least three edges. With at most six vertices this forces P1 to have exactly three edges, P2 to be one edge, and their union to contain every vertex. Q cannot be the terminal edge, so it has two edges. Its internal vertex is either internal to P1, making Q compatible with P2, or lies on P2, in which case Q's two incident edges contradict the absence of cross-edges. In the seven-vertex graph, s2t2 is forced and s1-x-t1 is uniquely shortest, so their total-length-three ordinary linkage is uniquely minimum but is non-induced because of xs2.
claims.witness: The same seven-vertex graph has unique ordinary minimum (s1-x-t1,s2-t2), while (s1-y-z-t1,s2-t2) is an induced linkage.
claims.search_method: Complete proof plus exhaustive enumeration of 2980224 graph/terminal instances through six vertices, including both choices of the designated first pair.

target_evidence: The exact source target asks for a complexity classification for every fixed k on all H3-subgraph-free graphs. The draft completely settles only k=1 and proves conditional, parameterized, structural, and obstruction results; it expressly withdraws the unrestricted represented-class conclusion and provides neither a standard-instance polynomial algorithm nor NP-hardness for any fixed k≥2. These are correct material advances but do not resolve the target, so PARTIAL is accurate.
